title: Bounded-above resolutions from a quotient-generating class
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $\mathcal P\subset\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal A)$ contain a zero object, and assume every object of $\mathcal A$ is a quotient of an object of $\mathcal P$. Let $a\in\mathbf Z$. If $K^\bullet$ is a cochain complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with $K^n=0$ for every $n>a$, then there exist a cochain complex $P^\bullet$ and a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ such that every $P^n$ lies in $\mathcal P$, every component $P^n\to K^n$ is an epimorphism, and $P^n=0$ for every $n>a$.

proof.text: Choose the supplied zero object Z in P, and for each object X choose a covering epimorphism pi_X:T(X) to X from hcover. These choices use only the hypotheses, not an unproved existence theorem. A stage stores its degree n, current and next objects, current differential d and augmentation e to K^n. The initial stage in degree a+1 uses Z for both objects and zero maps.

Given a stage in degree n, form W=K^{n-1} times_{K^n} kernel(d), with right map the kernel inclusion followed by e. The next current object is T(W); its differential is pi_W followed by the second projection and kernel inclusion, and its augmentation is pi_W followed by the first projection. The kernel equation proves square-zero, and the pullback equation proves compatibility with K. Iterate this explicit construction over the natural numbers, starting in degree a+1. For integer i at most a use stage depth (a-i).toNat+1; above a use the chosen Z. The equality of adjacent stage terms transports both equations to integer degrees, so CochainComplex.of and ofHom give L and f. All terms satisfy P by the choice of covers, or by P Z above a.

For i at most a, identify the assembled term L^i with T(K^i times_{K^{i+1}} kernel(d_L^{i+1})). The comparison to this pullback is epic, and its two projections are f^i and d_L^i by the step equations. Apply [lem-pc-functorial-cycle-pullback-lifting-stage3]: a cycle x:B to L^{i+1} and a compatible y:B to K^i admit, after an epimorphic refinement p:B prime to B, a simultaneous lift z:B prime to L^i with z f^i=p y and z d_L^i=p x. Above a both x and y are zero, so the same conclusion holds with p the identity and z zero. No functorial cover assumption is used.

Apply the mono and epi homology-map refinement criteria of [lem-sp-abelian-refinements], exposed for complexes by Mathlib Algebra.Homology.Refinements. For injectivity in degree i, a cycle x in L^i mapping to the boundary of y in K^{i-1} is handled by the simultaneous lifting property in degree i-1; the lift exhibits x as a boundary after refinement. For surjectivity, apply that property in degree i to x=0 and a cycle y in K^i; the resulting z is a cycle lifting y after refinement, with zero boundary correction. Thus every homology map is monic and epic, hence an isomorphism in the abelian category, and f is a quasi-isomorphism.

To prove f^i epic, take y:B to K^i. Apply the simultaneous lifting property in degree i+1 to the pair (0,y d_K^i), obtaining a cycle x in L^{i+1} after refinement p1. Apply the property in degree i to the compatible pair (x,p1 y). Its augmentation is p2 p1 y. The composite refinement is epic, so [lem-sp-abelian-refinements](a) gives Epi f^i. Together with the term property, the preserved upper bound and the quasi-isomorphism this is the conclusion.

lean.statement: theorem exists_subcategory_left_resolution {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] (P : C → Prop) (hzero : ∃ Z : C, P Z ∧ IsZero Z) (hcover : ∀ X : C, ∃ (Y : C) (p : Y ⟶ X), P Y ∧ Epi p) (a : ℤ) (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (hK : ∀ n : ℤ, a < n → IsZero (K.X n)) : ∃ (L : CochainComplex C ℤ) (f : L ⟶ K), QuasiIso f ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, P (L.X n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, Epi (f.f n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, a < n → IsZero (L.X n))
